library_items.title: Math Academy lesson
library_items.description: One or two lessons. Stop when the timer ends.

library_items.title: Math Academy review
library_items.description: Clear the review queue before starting anything new.

library_items.description: Half a test in 20 minutes. Circle the ones to revisit.

library_items.title: AMC 8 full practice test
library_items.description: 25 problems in 40 minutes, just like the real one.

library_items.title: Redo missed contest problems
library_items.description: Solve each again without looking. Then say why the first try went wrong.

library_items.title: Berkeley Math Circle puzzle
library_items.description: Pick one problem and chew on it. No answer needed.

library_items.title: Prepare the math club idea of the week
library_items.description: One idea, one example, one question for the club.

library_items.title: Explain one math idea out loud
library_items.description: Teach it to a parent, a grandparent or the dog.

library_items.title: Dice math: what does 2d6 really roll?
library_items.description: List every outcome, count them, draw the shape. Then test it with real dice.

library_items.title: Write a session recap
library_items.description: 150 to 250 words: what happened, in order, with one vivid detail. Send it to your players.

library_items.title: World bible: add one page
library_items.description: A place, a faction, a monster or a legend.

library_items.title: Outline the winter one-shot
library_items.description: A hook, three scenes, a twist and an ending. One page.

library_items.title: Write one encounter for the one-shot
library_items.description: What do the players want, what stands in the way, and what happens if they fail?

library_items.title: Draw a map for the adventure
Make three characters with a want and a secret
Revise a piece with the checklist
library_items.description: Is it clear? Is there one vivid detail in each scene? What can I cut?

library_items.title: Sentence-combining game
library_items.description: Take five short sentences from a recap. Turn them into two better ones.

library_items.title: Read a published adventure like a writer
library_items.description: Notice how it is organized. Borrow the structure, never the words.

library_items.title: Pixar in a Box storytelling lesson
library_items.description: One lesson, then use it on your villain or your plot.

library_items.title: Idea notebook: ten new ideas
library_items.description: Bad ideas count. Ten of anything.

library_items.title: Tell the grandparents the story so far
Practice a 60-second pitch
library_items.description: One clear point, one example, one ask.

library_items.title: Stone Soup piece: draft or revise
micro:bit: first programs
library_items.description: Show your name, a beating heart, and a dice roller on shake.

library_items.title: micro:bit: log data for an experiment
library_items.description: Write the question and your prediction before you press record.

library_items.title: Is my d20 fair? Roll and record 100 rolls
library_items.description: Tally every roll. Do it twice for 200.

library_items.title: Is my d20 fair? Chart it and give the verdict
library_items.description: One chart. How uneven is too uneven to be luck?

library_items.title: CreateAI: record drum strokes and train a model
library_items.description: At least three samples of each stroke. More is better.

library_items.title: CreateAI: test the model on someone else
library_items.description: Count right and wrong out of 20. Why does it miss?

library_items.title: Data story: one chart and 150 words
library_items.description: Question, data, one honest chart, what surprised me, who should do what.

library_items.title: Build something from what is in the house
library_items.description: Cardboard, LEGO, tape and string all count.

library_items.title: Take something apart (ask first)
library_items.description: Lay the parts out in order. Can you put it back?

library_items.title: STEM Fair: brainstorm ten questions
library_items.description: Things you could measure at home or at school.

library_items.title: STEM Fair: plan the test
library_items.description: What will you change, what will you measure, and how many times?

library_items.title: Calibration check
library_items.description: Compare a sensor with something you trust and write down the difference.

library_items.title: Catch the AI (with a parent)
library_items.description: Compare an AI monster description with your own. Which is better, and why?

library_items.title: Drums: rudiments with a metronome
library_items.description: Slow and even beats fast and messy.

library_items.title: Flute: long tones and a scale
Record a take and listen back
library_items.description: Pick one thing to fix next time.

library_items.title: Make drum cues or a soundtrack for the campaign
Arrow of Light: work on a requirement
Pack my own bag for an outing
Troop choice: what I liked about each troop
library_items.description: Three things for each. Which felt like your people?

library_items.title: Scout Oath and Law from memory
Fitness: push-ups, sit-ups and a run
Nature notebook or stargazing
library_items.description: Draw one thing you noticed and one question about it.

library_items.title: Call or video chat with a friend
Game or show time
library_items.description: Within our family media plan.

library_items.title: Laundry: wash, dry and fold my load
Cook one meal myself
library_items.description: With a parent nearby. You choose the recipe.

library_items.title: Pack for the trip
library_items.description: Make the list first, then pack from the list.

library_items.title: Help someone without being asked
library_items.description: Then tell us at dinner what you noticed.

library_items.title: Wind down: screens off, book in bed
Plan my week
library_items.description: Place the must-dos first, then your own picks. Leave room for nothing.

library_items.title: Weekly check-in with Mom and Dad
library_items.description: You lead it. What interested you? What was too easy or too hard? What do you want to stop?

library_items.title: Sort the Catch-up tray
library_items.description: For each card: new time, smaller, or ask to drop.

library_items.title: Update my ship log
library_items.description: Write down what you finished this month.

library_items.title: Pick next week's focus with a parent
library_items.description: Up to three things. They can change every week.

words.definition: Not giving up, even when something is hard.
words.example: The tenacious ranger tracked the wyvern through three nights of rain.

words.definition: Clear and easy to understand.
words.example: Her lucid explanation made the puzzle seem simple.

words.definition: To search for food or supplies.
words.example: The scouts foraged for dry wood before the storm.

words.definition: Very careful about small details.
words.example: A meticulous mapmaker measures every bend in the river.

words.definition: Able to be understood in more than one way.
words.example: The riddle's ambiguous clue sent half the party left and half right.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly after something goes wrong.
words.example: The resilient drummer missed a beat and came right back in.

words.definition: An idea you can test to see whether it is true.
words.example: My hypothesis is that the red die rolls high more often.

words.definition: Working steadily and carefully.
words.example: Diligent practice turned the hard measure into an easy one.

words.definition: To make something up on the spot.
words.example: When the players skipped the bridge, the Dungeon Master had to improvise.

words.definition: Not believing something until you see good evidence.
words.example: She was skeptical of the lucky dice until she counted the rolls.

words.definition: Speaking or writing in a clear, moving way.
words.example: The eloquent bard talked the guards into opening the gate.

words.definition: Exact and accurate.
words.example: A precise measurement needs the same ruler every time.

words.definition: To keep going in spite of difficulty.
words.example: They persevered up the last switchback to the summit.

words.definition: Suggesting that something bad is about to happen.
words.example: An ominous rumble came from under the old mill.

words.definition: To work together on something.
words.example: The patrol collaborated to pitch the tent before dark.

words.definition: Eager to learn and full of questions.
words.example: The inquisitive apprentice asked why the potion turned blue.

words.definition: Making a strong, clear picture in your mind.
words.example: One vivid detail, like the smell of smoke, makes a scene feel real.

words.definition: To figure something out from clues.
words.example: From the muddy prints she deduced that the thief had come by the river.

words.definition: To adjust a tool so that it measures correctly.
words.example: Calibrate the sensor before you trust its numbers.

words.definition: Saying a lot in few words.
words.example: A concise recap fits on one card.

words.definition: Impressive in a way that is a little frightening.
words.example: The dragon was a formidable opponent, even asleep.

words.definition: Seeming reasonable or likely to be true.
words.example: It was a plausible excuse, but the cookie crumbs told another story.

words.definition: To expect something and get ready for it.
words.example: Good planners anticipate rain and pack a tarp.

words.definition: The force that keeps something moving once it has started.
words.example: After three good days, the project had real momentum.

words.definition: Having many small parts or details.
words.example: The lock had an intricate pattern of gears.

words.definition: Honest and direct.
words.example: A candid friend tells you when your plan has a hole in it.

words.definition: A serious attempt to do something.
words.example: Building the treehouse was a summer-long endeavor.

words.definition: To study something closely in order to understand it.
words.example: Analyze the problems you missed before you try new ones.

words.definition: Quick and light in movement or thought.
words.example: The nimble rogue slipped past the trap.

words.definition: A person who is new to something.
words.example: Every expert drummer started as a novice.

words.definition: To change something in order to make it better.
words.example: Revise the ending so the villain's plan makes sense.

words.definition: Real enough to touch or measure.
words.example: A finished map is tangible proof of a week's work.

words.definition: Watching carefully for danger or problems.
words.example: The vigilant lookout spotted the smoke first.

words.definition: To combine parts into a new whole.
words.example: Synthesize your notes into one clear page.

words.definition: Needing a great deal of effort.
words.example: It was an arduous climb with full packs.

words.definition: Confused because something is hard to understand.
words.example: The perplexed wizard stared at the map that kept redrawing itself.

words.definition: Clever and original.
words.example: An ingenious pulley let one scout lift the whole food bag.

words.definition: Something that blocks your way.
words.example: Every good adventure puts an obstacle between the heroes and the goal.

words.definition: Wise and careful about the future.
words.example: It is prudent to check the weather before a hike.

words.definition: The feeling of being thankful.
words.example: He showed his gratitude with a handwritten note.

words.definition: To pause before acting because you are unsure.
words.example: Do not hesitate to ask when the directions are unclear.

words.definition: To make a careful guess about a number or an amount.
words.example: Estimate how long the task will take, then check afterward.

words.definition: Something that happens because of an action.
words.example: Skipping the map check had a soggy consequence.

words.definition: Able to do many different things well.
words.example: A versatile drummer can play jazz, rock and marching band.

words.definition: To become smaller or weaker.
words.example: The echo diminished as they left the cave.

words.definition: Present in large amounts.
words.example: Blackberries were abundant along the trail.

words.definition: To reach an agreement by talking.
words.example: The party negotiated a truce with the goblin chief.

words.definition: Expecting good things to happen.
words.example: She stayed optimistic about the second try.

words.definition: Facts that help show whether something is true.
words.example: Two hundred rolls gave him enough evidence to judge the die.

words.definition: To keep changing, up and down.
words.example: The temperature fluctuated all afternoon.

words.definition: Calmness, especially under pressure.
words.example: The Dungeon Master kept her composure when the plan fell apart.

words.definition: Having many carefully arranged details.
words.example: They built an elaborate fort from cardboard and tape.

words.definition: Not wanting to do something.
words.example: The reluctant hero finally picked up the sword.

words.definition: The power to start something on your own.
words.example: She took the initiative and organized the club's first game night.

words.definition: A hard choice between two options.
words.example: Save the village or chase the thief: a real dilemma.

words.definition: Something different from what is normal or expected.
words.example: One reading of ninety degrees was an anomaly in the data.

words.definition: Notes that sound good together; also, peaceful agreement.
words.example: The flute and the clarinet played in harmony.

words.definition: The speed of a piece of music.
words.example: Start at a slow tempo and speed up when it is clean.

words.definition: A gradual increase in loudness.
words.example: The drums built to a crescendo before the final chord.

words.definition: Rhythm that stresses the beats you do not expect.
words.example: Syncopation gives the groove its bounce.

words.definition: The shape and features of the land.
words.example: Check the terrain on the map before choosing a campsite.

words.definition: To find the way from one place to another.
words.example: They navigated by compass when the fog rolled in.

words.definition: The highest point of a mountain.
words.example: They reached the summit just before noon.

words.definition: To start a fire; also, to spark a feeling.
words.example: A good question can kindle a week of curiosity.

words.definition: To go somewhere or try something risky.
words.example: Few travelers venture past the broken bridge.

words.definition: Clever at getting what you want, sometimes by tricks.
words.example: The cunning fox led the hounds in circles.

words.definition: A long journey full of adventures.
words.example: Their trip to the science fair turned into an odyssey.

words.definition: Serious danger.
words.example: The map marked the swamp with one word: peril.

words.definition: Great courage in a hard moment.
words.example: The knight was remembered for valor, not for winning.

words.definition: Knowledge and stories passed down over time.
words.example: Every world needs lore: who built the ruins, and why.

words.definition: An object made by people long ago.
words.example: The artifact hummed when the moon rose.

words.definition: An agreement to work together.
words.example: The dwarves and the elves formed an uneasy alliance.

words.definition: How likely something is to happen.
words.example: The probability of rolling a 20 on a fair d20 is one in twenty.

words.definition: Something that can change in an experiment.
words.example: Change one variable at a time, or you will not know what caused the result.

words.definition: A link between two things that change together.
words.example: There was a correlation between practice time and clean takes.

words.definition: A match between two halves, like mirror images.
words.example: A snowflake has six-fold symmetry.

words.definition: Things that follow each other in a set order.
words.example: Find the next number in the sequence.

words.definition: A guess based on some evidence but not yet proven.
words.example: His conjecture was that the pattern would repeat every seven steps.

words.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence.
words.example: From the wet umbrella we can infer that it is raining.

words.definition: To make something as good or as efficient as possible.
words.example: Optimize the route so no one walks the same trail twice.

words.definition: A first version built to test an idea.
words.example: The cardboard prototype showed that the handle was too short.

words.definition: To repeat a process, improving it each time.
words.example: Build, test, fix, and iterate.

words.definition: Getting a lot done with little waste.
words.example: An efficient packer fits a week of gear in one bag.

words.definition: Understanding how someone else feels.
words.example: Empathy helped him see why his teammate was upset.

words.definition: Being honest and doing what is right, even when no one is watching.
words.example: Marking a card half done when it was half done takes integrity.

words.definition: Not thinking you are better than other people.
words.example: The champion stayed humble and thanked her coach.

words.definition: Happy to give or share.
words.example: He was generous with his time and taught the new scout three knots.

words.definition: Loyal and not easily changed.
words.example: A steadfast friend shows up on moving day.

words.definition: Responsible for what you do and willing to explain it.
words.example: A patrol leader is accountable for the whole patrol's gear.

words.definition: Done on purpose and with thought.
words.example: Slow, deliberate practice beats fast, sloppy practice.

words.definition: Something that matters more than other things.
words.example: Sleep is a priority, even on game night.

words.definition: To put off something you should do.
words.example: He procrastinated until the tray was full.

words.definition: To think carefully about something that happened.
words.example: Reflect on the week: what would you keep?

words.definition: The freedom to make your own choices.
words.example: With autonomy comes the job of planning your own time.

words.definition: To aim for something great.
words.example: She aspires to design her own game.

words.definition: A story, or the way a story is told.
words.example: A good chart has a narrative: a question, a surprise and an answer.

words.definition: The main character of a story.
words.example: The protagonist wants something, and something stands in the way.

words.definition: To hint at what will happen later in a story.
words.example: The cracked bell foreshadowed the fall of the tower.

words.definition: The words characters say to each other.
words.example: Dialogue shows who a character is faster than description does.

words.definition: The most exciting and important moment of a story.
words.example: The climax came when the bridge began to burn.

encouragements.text: A plan is a map, not a cage. Pick your first card and go.
Small steps add up. What is the smallest one you can take right now?
Start with the card you least want to do. The rest of the day gets lighter.
Half done is still half done. Mark it honestly and move on.
You are the one who decides what today looks like.
A finished small thing beats an unfinished big thing.
Stuck? Shrink the task until it fits in ten minutes.
Slow and even beats fast and messy. Ask any drummer.
Every expert was once a beginner who kept showing up.
Leave some room in the day for nothing at all.
Mistakes are data. What did this one tell you?
The tray is not a failure pile. It is a list of second chances.
Do one thing today that next week's you will thank you for.
A good Dungeon Master prepares, then improvises. So does a good planner.
You do not have to feel ready to start.
Curiosity first. What do you want to find out today?
Rest is part of the plan, not a break from it.
If the plan is not working, change the plan, not the goal.
One card at a time. The board will still be here.
Did something go well yesterday? Do more of that.
Ask for help early. It is a skill, not a weakness.
Hard is not the same as bad. Hard is where the growing happens.
Be the kind of teammate you would want in your party.
Look at what is already in Done. That is progress you can see.
Estimate, then check. Your guesses get better every week.
Closing out the day takes two minutes. Tomorrow's you will be glad.
You can do difficult things for a short time. Set a timer.
Leave it better than you found it: your room, your work, your campsite.
A question you cannot answer yet is the start of a project.
Nobody rolls a 20 every time. Play the roll you got.
Notice one thing you did well today, and one thing to try differently.
Kindness counts. Who could you help today without being asked?
Protect your sleep. Everything works better after it.
Finish, then polish. Not the other way around.
It is okay to drop something. Do it on purpose, not by accident.
The first draft is allowed to be bad. That is its job.
Practice is where you are allowed to sound terrible.
Read something today just because you want to.
Go outside. Ideas like fresh air.
You have done hard things before. This is one more.
What would make today feel like a good day? Plan that in.
Explain it out loud. If you can teach it, you know it.
Trade perfect for done, then make it better tomorrow.
A streak is nice. Starting again after a miss is nicer.
Do the must-dos first, then the day is yours.
Check twice, then trust it.
Good adventures have obstacles. So do good weeks.
Pack your bag the night before. Plan your day the same way.
Be honest with the board. It only helps if it is true.
Too much on today? Move something. That is what the week is for.
Your ideas are yours. Write one down before it gets away.
Listen first. The best players and the best leaders do.
Take the next step, not all the steps.
You get better at what you repeat. Choose what you repeat.
Being bored is where good ideas start.
Say thank you to someone today.
One good question is worth ten quick answers.
Check in with yourself: tired, hungry, or just stuck?
Celebrate the finish. Then pick the next quest.
Today is a fresh page.
